objectives.title: Objective A: Managing Cyber Risk
objectives.description: Appropriate organisational structures, policies, and processes in place to understand, assess and systematically manage cyber security risks to essential functions.

principles.title: Governance
principles.description: The organisation has appropriate governance structures in place to manage cyber security risks to essential functions.

outcomes.title: Board Direction
outcomes.description: The board or equivalent senior leadership directs and oversees the management of cyber risk to essential functions.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Senior leadership understands cyber risk and regularly reviews cyber posture.

igps.description: The board demonstrates active oversight of cyber risk, sets risk appetite for citizen services, and reviews quarterly reports.
The board discusses cyber security reactively after major incidents without formal strategic risk appetite metrics.

outcomes.title: Roles and Responsibilities
outcomes.description: Clear roles and responsibilities are defined and allocated to appropriately skilled individuals.
outcomes.guidance_notes: A designated individual (e.g. CISO / SIRO) has formal responsibility for cyber security.

igps.description: A formally appointed CISO or cyber lead has explicit authority, budget, and resources for council-wide cyber posture.
Cyber security roles are assigned informally to general IT support without designated accountability.

outcomes.title: Decision-making
outcomes.description: Cyber security is integrated into organisational decision-making, including project governance and procurement.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Security gates exist for all digital procurement and architectural changes.

igps.description: Cyber security risk assessments and sign-offs are mandatory gates in all IT procurement and cloud migrations.
Security advice is sought informally but projects can be deployed without formal sign-off.

principles.title: Risk Management
principles.description: The organisation takes an active, risk-based approach to identifying and managing risks to essential functions.

outcomes.title: Risk Management Process
outcomes.description: A dynamic risk management process identifies, analyses, prioritises, and tracks cyber security risks.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Risks to essential citizen services are continually evaluated.

igps.description: A dynamic cyber risk management framework actively tracks threats and system vulnerabilities.
Risk management relies on static annual reviews without active monitoring of threat likelihood.

outcomes.title: Understanding Threat
outcomes.description: The organisation understands the cyber threat landscape as it applies to its essential functions.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Threat intelligence is tracked from NCSC, CiSP, and sector advisories.

igps.description: Threat intelligence feeds and sector bulletins are reviewed continuously to assess threat actor capabilities against council infrastructure.
Threat awareness is generic and does not evaluate specific tactics targeting local authorities.

outcomes.title: Assurance
outcomes.description: The organisation gains confidence that its cyber risk management processes and controls are effective.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Third-party penetration testing and technical audits validate defenses.

igps.description: Regular independent CREST/CHECK penetration tests and external audits validate control effectiveness.
Assurance is based solely on self-assessment without technical testing or independent validation.

principles.title: Asset Management
principles.description: The organisation understands, documents, and manages the assets that support its essential functions.

outcomes.title: Asset Management
outcomes.description: Everything which plays a role in delivering essential functions is inventoried and understood.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Hardware, software, data, cloud workloads, and operational dependencies are tracked.

igps.description: Automated asset discovery maintains an accurate real-time inventory of all hardware, cloud instances, and systems.
Asset registers exist in static spreadsheets with untracked shadow IT assets.

principles.title: Supply Chain
principles.description: The organisation understands and manages security risks arising from its supply chains.

outcomes.title: Supply Chain
outcomes.description: Supply chain dependencies and risks to essential functions are understood and governed.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Key suppliers (cloud MSPs, software vendors) are risk-tiered.

igps.description: All third-party suppliers are categorized by risk tier with contractual security requirements and audit rights.
Key suppliers are known, but supply chain security relies on vendor trust without contractual validation.

outcomes.title: Secure Software Development and Support
outcomes.description: Security requirements are enforced for custom software and ongoing vendor software support.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Secure SDLC practices and SLA commitments for vulnerability patching.

igps.description: Software vendors and internal development adhere to secure coding standards with vulnerability patching SLAs.
Software security is reviewed only when major vulnerabilities are publicly disclosed.

objectives.title: Objective B: Protecting Against Cyber Attack
objectives.description: Proportionate security measures are in place to protect networks and information systems supporting essential functions from cyber attack.

principles.title: Service Protection Policies and Processes
principles.description: The organisation defines, approves, and communicates security policies and processes.

outcomes.title: Policy, Process and Procedure Development
outcomes.description: Security policies and procedures are developed, documented, and reviewed annually.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Policies cover IAM, encryption, remote working, and vulnerability management.

igps.description: Security policies are documented, aligned with NCSC guidelines, approved by leadership, and reviewed annually.
Policies exist but are outdated or not systematically reviewed against emerging threats.

outcomes.title: Policy, Process and Procedure Implementation
outcomes.description: Security policies and processes are effectively implemented across the council.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Automated configuration and policy enforcement.

igps.description: Policy compliance is automated and validated using technical controls and configuration management.
Policies are communicated to staff, but compliance relies on manual adherence without technical guardrails.

principles.title: Identity and Access Control
principles.description: Access to networks, systems, and data is understood, controlled, and restricted to authorised users.

outcomes.title: Identity Verification, Authentication and Authorisation
outcomes.description: Users and services are uniquely identified and authenticated with strong controls.
outcomes.guidance_notes: MFA on all remote endpoints and cloud identity providers.

igps.description: Phishing-resistant MFA is strictly enforced for all user accounts, remote access, and cloud portals.
MFA is enforced on external VPN, but internal administrative portals allow single-factor login.

outcomes.title: Device Management
outcomes.description: All user devices accessing council networks and systems are controlled and compliant.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Corporate MDM/Intune deployment with device compliance checks.

igps.description: All corporate and mobile devices are enrolled in MDM, enforcing health checks and encryption.
Unmanaged personal devices can connect to council webmail and cloud files without conditional access.

outcomes.title: Privileged User Management
outcomes.description: Privileged accounts are strictly separated and managed under least-privilege principles.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Dedicated admin accounts and JIT elevation.

igps.description: Privileged accounts are strictly separate from daily user accounts with just-in-time elevation and logging.
Staff use administrative credentials on standard email and web browsing workstations.

outcomes.title: Identity and Access Management (IdAM)
outcomes.description: Access permissions are systematically provisioned, reviewed, and promptly revoked.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Automated offboarding and regular entitlement reviews.

igps.description: Access rights are granted on least-privilege, reviewed quarterly, and revoked immediately upon leaver notification.
Offboarding is manual, leading to orphan accounts and lingering permissions.

principles.title: Data Security
principles.description: Data at rest and in transit is protected from unauthorised access, disclosure, and modification.

outcomes.title: Understanding Data
outcomes.description: The organisation understands the data it processes, stores, and transmits.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Classification of sensitive citizen data.

igps.description: Data classification is enforced with automated DLP identifying sensitive citizen records.
Classification guidelines exist on paper but are not applied to unstructured data repositories.

outcomes.title: Data in Transit
outcomes.description: Data in transit is protected from interception, eavesdropping, and tampering.
outcomes.guidance_notes: TLS 1.2+ minimum, IPsec VPNs, deprecated cipher suites disabled.

igps.description: Modern cryptographic protocols (TLS 1.2+) are enforced on all network communications.
External traffic is encrypted, but legacy cleartext protocols persist internally.

outcomes.title: Stored Data
outcomes.description: Data at rest is protected against unauthorised physical or logical access.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Full-disk encryption (BitLocker/FileVault) and encrypted database volumes.

igps.description: All laptops, databases, and server volumes enforce AES-256 encryption at rest.
Laptops are encrypted, but on-premise file shares and databases remain unencrypted.

outcomes.title: Mobile Data
outcomes.description: Mobile devices and remote workers handle council data securely.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Remote wipe capability and device containerisation.

igps.description: Mobile devices enforce encryption, secure containers, and instant remote wipe capabilities.
Mobile devices can store council files locally without containerisation or remote wipe.

outcomes.title: Media/Equipment Sanitisation
outcomes.description: Removable media and decommissioned hardware are securely handled and sanitized.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Certified disposal standards (ADISA) and USB block policies.

igps.description: Removable media is blocked by policy, and end-of-life media undergoes certified destruction.
Removable media is permitted without encryption, and disposal relies on standard recycling.

principles.title: System Security
principles.description: Networks and information systems are designed, configured, maintained, and operated securely.

outcomes.title: Secure by Design
outcomes.description: Systems are architected to minimise attack surface and isolate critical functions.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Network segmentation isolating citizen databases and core workloads.

igps.description: Network architecture enforces zero-trust segmentation isolating Tier 1 citizen databases.
The internal network is largely flat, allowing lateral movement from user PCs to servers.

outcomes.title: Secure Configuration
outcomes.description: Systems are hardened according to recognised security baselines.
outcomes.guidance_notes: CIS Benchmarks or NCSC configuration standards applied.

igps.description: CIS hardening baselines are applied automatically and audited for compliance drift.
Systems use default vendor settings with ad-hoc manual hardening.

outcomes.title: Secure Management
outcomes.description: Administrative tools and management interfaces are isolated and hardened.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Dedicated management network and Privileged Access Workstations.

igps.description: Management is performed from dedicated Privileged Access Workstations with internet isolation.
Administrators manage core infrastructure from general desktop workstations.

outcomes.title: Vulnerability Management
outcomes.description: Vulnerabilities are discovered, prioritised, and remediated within defined SLAs.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Regular authenticated vulnerability scanning and patch SLAs.

igps.description: Automated weekly vulnerability scans run with critical vulnerabilities patched within 14 days.
Patching occurs monthly without formal vulnerability scanning of internal networks.

principles.title: Resilient Networks and Systems
principles.description: Networks and information systems are designed to withstand failures and recover rapidly.

outcomes.title: Resilience Preparation
outcomes.description: Resilience requirements for essential services are understood, planned, and resourced.
outcomes.guidance_notes: RTO and RPO defined for statutory council services.

igps.description: Formal Recovery Time and Point Objectives (RTO/RPO) are defined and tested for all essential services.
Disaster recovery is planned informally without agreed service-specific recovery time objectives.

outcomes.title: Design for Resilience
outcomes.description: System architecture eliminates single points of failure for essential functions.
outcomes.guidance_notes: High-availability clustering, dual circuits, and diverse power supplies.

igps.description: Essential infrastructure is deployed with high availability, redundant paths, and multi-region failover.
Critical services rely on single switches, firewalls, or physical servers with no redundancy.

outcomes.title: Backups
outcomes.description: Immutable, isolated backups are maintained and verified against ransomware attacks.
outcomes.guidance_notes: 3-2-1 backup strategy with immutable offsite copies.

igps.description: Immutable, air-gapped backups follow the 3-2-1 rule with automated quarterly test restores.
Backups are stored on domain-joined storage vulnerable to ransomware encryption.

principles.title: Staff Awareness and Training
principles.description: Staff receive appropriate cyber security awareness and role-specific training.

outcomes.title: Cyber Security Culture
outcomes.description: A positive, supportive cyber security culture is promoted throughout the council.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Blameless incident reporting and strong security culture.

igps.description: Annual mandatory training achieves >95% completion with simulated phishing and proactive reporting.
Training is delivered once at induction with no ongoing refresher awareness campaigns.

outcomes.title: Cyber Security Training
outcomes.description: Personnel in high-risk, IT, or leadership roles receive tailored security training.
outcomes.guidance_notes: System admins and crisis leaders receive specialised training.

igps.description: Privileged admins and incident response leads complete role-specific security certifications and training.
Administrators receive generic staff training without advanced security engineering coursework.

objectives.title: Objective C: Detecting Cyber Security Events
objectives.description: Capabilities in place to detect cyber security events that could affect the delivery of essential functions.

principles.title: Security Monitoring
principles.description: Continuous monitoring is in place across network and system endpoints.

outcomes.title: Sources and Tools for Logging and Monitoring
outcomes.description: Logging covers all critical networks, endpoints, identity providers, and cloud workloads.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Centralized SIEM or MDR collecting telemetry.

igps.description: A centralized SIEM/MDR ingests logs across cloud tenants, domain controllers, perimeters, and EDR agents.
Logs are retained locally on individual servers without centralized aggregation or correlation.

outcomes.title: Securing Logs
outcomes.description: Security logs and audit records are protected against tampering and unauthorized deletion.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Immutable write-once storage for audit logs.

igps.description: Logs are shipped in real-time to append-only, tamper-evident cloud storage with restricted access.
Logs are accessible to standard administrators and can be altered or erased without alerting.

outcomes.title: Generating Alerts
outcomes.description: Alerting logic promptly flags anomalous and malicious security events.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Rules tuned to detect credential abuse, lateral movement, and ransomware activity.

igps.description: Automated correlation rules mapped to MITRE ATT&CK generate real-time high-priority alerts.
Alerting generates high false-positive noise with no active correlation of multi-stage attacks.

outcomes.title: Triage of Security Alerts
outcomes.description: Alerts are investigated and triaged by skilled analysts according to defined SLAs.
outcomes.guidance_notes: 24/7 SOC or rapid daytime escalation paths.

igps.description: A 24/7 SOC or MDR service triages critical alerts within 15 minutes with defined escalation runbooks.
Alerts are reviewed only during business hours, leaving evenings and weekends unmonitored.

principles.title: Proactive Security Event Discovery
principles.description: Active discovery capabilities identify anomalies, hidden compromises, and indicators of compromise.

outcomes.title: Threat Hunting and Discovery
outcomes.description: Proactive hunting and automated discovery tools identify unknown or anomalous activity.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Proactive threat hunting and indicators of compromise matching.

igps.description: Threat hunters and EDR telemetry actively sweep the environment for stealthy adversaries and IOCs.
Detection is purely reactive to automated signature alerts without proactive threat hunting.

objectives.title: Objective D: Minimising the Impact of Cyber Security Incidents
objectives.description: Capabilities in place to respond effectively to cyber security incidents and restore essential functions.

principles.title: Response and Recovery Planning
principles.description: Documented incident response and disaster recovery plans are prepared and regularly tested.

outcomes.title: Response Plan
outcomes.description: An Incident Response Plan defines escalation paths, communication channels, and statutory duties.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Includes ICO 72-hour notification, MHCLG/NCSC escalation, and crisis communications.

igps.description: A comprehensive Cyber Incident Response Plan details roles, out-of-band comms, and statutory reporting.
A generic disaster recovery document exists without specific playbooks for ransomware or data breaches.

outcomes.title: Response and Recovery Capability
outcomes.description: The organisation possesses the resources, tools, and third-party support to execute response plans.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Retained emergency incident response provider and forensic tooling.

igps.description: An emergency incident response retainer with a CREST-accredited DFIR firm is active with SLA response.
The council relies entirely on internal IT staff without external specialist DFIR retainer support.

outcomes.title: Testing and Exercising
outcomes.description: Incident response and disaster recovery plans are regularly tested through realistic exercises.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Annual tabletop exercises with executive and operational teams.

igps.description: Simulated cyber crisis tabletop exercises involving the Chief Executive and IT team occur at least annually.
Technical backups are tested, but leadership has never participated in a simulated cyber tabletop.

principles.title: Improvements
principles.description: Lessons learned from incidents and exercises feed back into improving cyber resilience.

outcomes.title: Post Incident Analysis
outcomes.description: Root cause analyses of incidents and exercises are documented and reviewed.
outcomes.guidance_notes: Formal post-incident review (PIR) meetings and reports.

igps.description: Post-incident reviews are mandatory following any major event, producing root-cause analysis and board reports.
Lessons are discussed informally within IT without documented root-cause findings or executive reporting.

outcomes.title: Using Incidents to Drive Improvements
outcomes.description: Remediation actions identified from incidents are tracked, funded, and implemented.
outcomes.guidance_notes: PIR action items assigned to named owners with agreed target dates.

igps.description: PIR recommendations are converted into funded remediation tasks tracked until closure on the risk register.
Remediation actions are identified, but implementation stalls due to lack of assigned budget or ownership.
